text:
I'd set this up in two stages. First I need you to confirm three things, then I'll run the commands.

**Confirm first:**
1. **Admin access.** GitHub runner registration needs admin on the repo. Is `acme-dev` an admin of `acme/webapp`? If not, setup will fail at the token step.
2. **Token on this laptop.** Setup makes this laptop a broker that holds the `acme-dev` token in the macOS keychain. Workers on your tailnet never see it. Is that OK?
3. **Workflow files.** I'd run `migrate` as a report first, so you can read what it would change in `.github/workflows` before anything is edited. Should I stop there, or write the changes too? Jobs that deploy, publish, sign or use environments are left alone either way. Which checkout path should I use?

**Commands, once you confirm:**

```sh
# 1. Install the binary only (sudo puts it in /usr/local/bin, where sudo can find it)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baney75/tentmaker/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- --no-setup
tentmaker version --json

# 2. Set up. No TTY, so every answer is a flag.
#    Everyday: 2 GiB, one job at a time, so your work isn't affected.
#    Plugged in: up to 16 GiB.
#    On battery: no new jobs.
#    The token comes from gh as the user who ran sudo, so nothing is piped.
sudo tentmaker setup --yes --json --repo acme/webapp --memory 2GiB --boost-memory 16GiB --on-battery off

# 3. Verify. Apply each fix it prints, then rerun until this exits 0.
tentmaker doctor --json

# 4. Report only, no edits (use --platform macos if the jobs need macOS)
tentmaker migrate ~/path/to/webapp --json
```

Once you've read the report and say yes, I'd run `tentmaker migrate ~/path/to/webapp --write --json`, review `git diff`, and commit on a branch. Nothing gets pushed without your go-ahead.

Two things to know. Jobs from fork pull requests never run on this laptop, whatever the workflow says. And the budget only shifts to 16 GiB while the charger is connected.
